chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr and Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

For every salat there are two times, and the first of the two times is the more excellent of them. The time of Salat al-Fajr is when the dawn breaks until the morning light spreads over the sky, and it is not proper to delay that deliberately; rather, that is the time of one who was occupied, or forgot, or was heedless, or slept. And the time of al-Maghrib is when the sun becomes concealed until the stars become intermingled; so it is not for anyone to make the latter of the two times his time except due to an excuse or an ailment.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُهُمَا: the more excellent or more virtuous of the two
key_terms.الصُّبْحُ: morning light spreading in the sky
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn, marking the beginning of Fajr prayer time
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset prayer and its appointed time
key_terms.الْوَقْتَيْنِ: the two time-periods for performing a prayer

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the preferred time for Fajr and Maghrib prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that each salat has a preferred earlier time and a later extension. It specifies the time ranges for Salat al-Fajr and al-Maghrib, and states that intentionally delaying prayer to the latter time is not appropriate except in cases of excuse or illness.
